1 حَاشَ الصَّيْدَ , (S, A, K,) aor. يَحُوشُ, (S,) inf. n. حَوْشٌ and حِيَاشٌ, (TA,) He came around the chase, or game, to turn it towards the snare; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ أَحَاشَهُ , and ↓ أَحْوَشَهُ , (S, K,) inf. n. إِحَاشَةٌ and إِحْوَاشٌ. (TA.) ―
-b2- حُشْتُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّيْدَ I aided him to hunt, or catch, the chase, or game; as also عليه ↓ أَحَشْتُهُ , and ↓ أَحْوَشْتُهُ عليه, and أَحْوَشْتُهُ إِيَّاهُ, on the authority of Th: (TA:) and حَاشَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّيْدَ He scared the chase, or game, towards him, and drove and collected it to him; as also ↓ احاشهُ . (TA.) ―
-b3- حَاشَ الذِّئْبُ الغَنَمَ The wolf drove along the sheep or goats. (TA.) ―
-b4- حَاشَ الإِبِلَ He collected together, and drove, the camels. (S, K.) ―
-b5- حَاشَهُ, inf. n. حَوْشٌ, also signifies [simply] He collected it; drew it together. (TA.) [See also 2.] ―
-b6- هُوَ يَحُوشُ الطَّعَامَ, (A,) inf. n. حَوْشٌ, (K,) He eats from the sides of the food so as to consume it: (A, K:) from IF. (TA.) ＝
-A2- [See also 7.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
